newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's NNPC wants bigger local crude allocation.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's NNPC wants bigger local crude allocation.

text.p: Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) on Thursday said it wanted the local allocation of crude oil increased to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 250,000 bpd at present.

"We are working to make the government realise that the 250,000 bpd it allocates for domestic refining is insufficient," Haruna Abubakar, managing director of NNPC subsidiary the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company, told journalists in Lagos.
Last month Nigeria cut the crude allocation from 300,000 bpd to 250,000 bpd.
Nigeria's four problem-plagued refineries are currently running at about the 250,000 bpd of the allocation out of a capacity of 445,000 bpd.
The managing director of the largest refinery at Port Harcourt told Reuters on Wednesday that processing could be increased to 320,000 bpd next year if the government spends money on the refineries.
Despite producing around two million bpd of crude Nigeria frequently resorts to imports when technical problems at the refineries create local shortages.
